result.summary: Independently reproduced both halves of TEST-DESIGNER's claim rather than trusting the report. (1) POST-FIX: ran `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` on this branch HEAD (c0ebde9) myself -- `Result: 15 passed`, 0 failures, quoted directly from my own terminal. (2) FAIL-THEN-PASS: rather than re-running the reported worktree measurement verbatim, I verified the pre-fix failure mode is genuinely structural by two independent methods. First, read `git show 99ec378:lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex` directly: `handoff_files/0` is `defp` (private, arity 0, globs only `**/*.json`), no `handoff_kind` function exists at all, and `lint_file/2` is `defp` (private) -- so calling `LintHandoffs.handoff_files/1`, `LintHandoffs.handoff_kind/1`, or `LintHandoffs.lint_file/2` externally would raise UndefinedFunctionError. Second, I actually invoked these functions against the compiled pre-fix module: `git worktree add ../letflow-tdv-prefix-check 99ec378`, then `MIX_ENV=test MIX_TEST_PARTITION=999 mix run --no-start -e '...'` compiling `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex` from that worktree and calling `function_exported?/3` plus live calls wrapped in `try/rescue`. Output: `handoff_files/1 exported?: false`, `handoff_kind/1 exported?: false`, `lint_file/2 exported?: false`, and all three live calls raised `UndefinedFunctionError`. This independently confirms TEST-DESIGNER's reported pre-fix failure mode (UndefinedFunctionError for exactly these three entry points) is real and structural, not copied. Note: this worktree run shared `_build`/`deps` with the main tree via MIX_DEPS_PATH/MIX_BUILD_PATH and briefly overwrote the compiled beam for this module with the pre-fix (stale) version in the shared `_build` cache; I caught this, ran `touch lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex && mix compile` to force recompilation from the real (post-fix) source, and reran the full test file to confirm `Result: 15 passed` again post-restore -- the shared build cache was not left stale. Worktree removed via `git worktree remove --force` immediately after measurement; `git worktree list` afterward shows only the main tree. (3) FIXTURE SELF-SUFFICIENCY: read `test/fixtures/lint_handoffs/h6/step-01-fixture-non-json.md` -- a static, committed, content-irrelevant file living outside `handoffs/`, never mutated by anything else in the repo; no dependency on shared state. (4) REAL-CORPUS ASSERTION ROBUSTNESS: verified empirically, not just by reading the code, that F-GRANDFATHERED-COUNT/DISCOVERED fail loudly (not silently pass) if the 10 grandfathered files go missing -- moved `handoffs/WF03-ISS0258-20260822/step-01-issue-fixer.md` aside, reran the suite: `Result: 13/15 passed` with F-GRANDFATHERED-COUNT and F-GRANDFATHERED-DISCOVERED both failing (F-GRANDFATHERED-NOT-NEW does not itself check disk presence, since `lint_file/2`'s `:non_json` branch is extension-only and never calls `File.read`, but COUNT's `Enum.all?(&File.regular?/1)` and DISCOVERED's dependency on `handoff_files/1`'s own `File.regular?/1` filter both catch the drift, so the describe block as a whole is robust). Restored the file and reran: `Result: 15 passed` again. `git status --porcelain` on the real tree after all maneuvers shows only this handoff file's own edit -- `handoffs/` content is unmutated, worktree cleaned up, no stray artifacts. All four acceptance criteria met; PASS.
